sections.title: Global Equities
sections.content: Global equities fell as renewed US-Iran hostilities pushed oil above **$100**, reviving inflation fears and lifting bond yields ahead of next week's FOMC. MSCI World slipped roughly **0.8%**, with MSCI Developed Markets similar and MSCI Emerging Markets down around **1.5%**. The S&P 500 lost **0.8%** to **7,656.98**, while the MAG7 mega-cap cohort was mixed and led Friday's rebound. Euro Stoxx 50 eased about **1.0%** to roughly **6,325**, China's CSI 300 fell **0.83%** to **4,510.16**, Hong Kong's Hang Seng tumbled **3.3%** and Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped **1.55%** to **64,011.34**.

sections.title: US Equities
sections.content:
US equities ended lower in a choppy week, with the S&P 500 down **0.8%** to **7,656.98** and the Dow and Nasdaq also softer, though all three snapped a four-day losing streak with a firm Friday session.

The dominant driver was Friday's August CPI report, which showed headline inflation at **3.4%** year on year and core at **2.4%**. Sticky prices, compounded by renewed US-Iran hostilities that lifted crude above **$100**, reinforced expectations that the Fed could raise rates at next week's FOMC, an unusually hawkish backdrop that weighed on sentiment through midweek.

Leadership on Friday's bounce favoured cyclicals and growth, with technology, industrials and communication services each rising over **1%** while healthcare and utilities lagged. Despite the pullback, the S&P 500 held near **11.9%** higher year to date, supported by 2026 earnings still tracking growth above **30%** and resilient business investment.

sections.title: European Equities
sections.content:
European bourses came under pressure as the oil-driven inflation scare and rising global yields sapped risk appetite. The MSCI Europe ex-UK Index fell about **1.0%** and the Euro Stoxx 50 eased to roughly **6,325**, underperforming a steadier late-week Wall Street.

The catalyst was early-week escalation in the US-Iran conflict, which drove crude and European natural gas prices higher, fuelling inflation concerns and pushing sovereign bond yields up across the region. Duration-sensitive and rate-exposed sectors bore the brunt of the sell-off.

Regional dispersion persisted, with energy and defence names relatively resilient against the weaker macro backdrop, while consumer-facing and rate-sensitive shares lagged. Attention stayed on the ECB's reaction function as energy-led price pressures complicated the path for policy.

sections.title: APAC Equities
sections.content:
Asian equities fell broadly as higher global yields and elevated oil prices weighed on risk sentiment. Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped **1.55%** to **64,011.34** and the broader TOPIX also declined, as rising Japanese government bond yields and mounting expectations of near-term BoJ tightening pressured highly valued growth stocks.

A sharp strengthening of the yen later in the week added to the drag on exporters. In China, the CSI 300 slipped **0.83%** to **4,510.16**, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng underperformed sharply, tumbling **3.3%** as offshore tech and property names gave back gains.

The common thread was tension between firmer policy-tightening bets in Japan and a more cautious China tone, with rising developed-market yields, the tech cycle and BoJ signals framing the regional outlook.

sections.title: Foreign Exchange
sections.content:
The US dollar firmed as the inflation scare and safe-haven demand revived expectations of a Fed rate hike, reversing part of the currency's softer tone earlier in the month. EUR/USD slipped to around **1.1597**, near its weakest level in over a week, as much of the pair's recent strength had reflected dollar weakness rather than euro-specific drivers.

Sterling held within a tight range near **1.35**, consolidating after a recent six-month high against the dollar. The standout was the yen, which strengthened sharply late in the week toward the mid-**154** area on firmer BoJ tightening bets, bucking the broader dollar recovery.

Convera highlighted that rising long-end yields have become a global phenomenon, reflecting fiscal-sustainability concerns, while energy-led eurozone inflation and shifting Fed expectations dominated near-term FX direction.

sections.title: Commodities
sections.content:
Energy was the dominant theme as renewed US-Iran hostilities stoked supply fears. Brent crude broke above **$100** and finished the week near **$104.61**, with both Brent and WTI gaining more than **8%**, reviving inflation concerns just as bond yields climbed.

Precious metals retreated as higher real yields and a firmer dollar undercut inflation hedges. Gold settled around **$4,348**, down close to **1%** on the week for a third consecutive weekly loss, while silver fell to about **$64.39**.

Industrial metals also softened: copper touched a record midweek on tight supply and US tariff expectations before retreating alongside the broader metals complex. The cross-asset read was clear, with geopolitics keeping energy bid even as rate-hike fears pressured metals, complicating the inflation outlook.

sections.title: Fixed Income
sections.content:
Sovereign yields rose as the inflation data and surging oil prices lifted rate-hike expectations. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about **4.97%**, while the 2-year topped **4.6%**, its highest since July 2024, reflecting a hawkish repricing of the near-term Fed path.

August CPI at **3.4%** headline and **2.4%** core, arriving alongside crude above **$100**, pushed markets to price a greater chance of a rate increase at the following week's FOMC meeting. The front-end-led move kept the curve under pressure as investors reassessed the policy outlook.

Edward Jones noted that resilient fundamentals still underpin the longer-term backdrop, citing 2026 S&P 500 earnings growth above **30%** and a firm labour market. Credit tone stayed broadly steady, with IG spreads resilient and HY holding up, though richer valuations and rate uncertainty argued for selectivity.
